newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE robusta futures near 4 pct up, extend rally.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE robusta futures near 4 pct up, extend rally.

text.p: London robusta coffee futures scaled a new one-year high on Wednesday as manufacturers scrambled to cover their positions with the current rally showing no signs of nearing its top.
By Wednesday midsession, prices were, however, off their peaks on origin offers, after having advanced by nearly four percent on the day.
Benchmark July, aided by further fund buying, carved a new one-year ceiling at $1,885 a tonne before settling the morning trade $55 up at $1,872.
London's surge came on the back of another steep gain in New York arabicas on Tuesday, which saw July hitting a 34-month high on supply shortages.
Traders said robustas were poised for further upward progress, with the initial upside objective seen at $1,920-$30 region. Support is seen intact at $1,800.
"We are at the end of hedging season from the Far East and Ivory Coast, so the pressure is off a bit," said one trader.
Despite the headway in London, the market continued to trail New York, whose prices have doubled in five months on tight arabica supplies from Central and South America.
"London is so far behind New York. Everyone is waking up to see how cheap robusta is," the same trader said.
July/July arbitrage against London stood at $1.56 cents a lb on Tuesday.
Immediately, the market is bracing for frost scares from Brazil as winter sets in from late May.
Brokerage GNI said that, as it had often noted, "a frost this year would cause chaos in the world coffee markets, with producer and consumer stocks at low levels".

Elsewhere, sources in Indonesia said next week's meeting of key coffee producers in London was expected to delay taking a decision over fresh export quotas in view of gains in prices. -- Jalil Hamid, London Newsroom +44 171 542 4985
